name: manual_6e1ac3
claim: GitHub stacked PRs: a stack is a chain where each PR's base is the branch of the PR below it and the bottom targets trunk; it needs a fully linear history and merges bottom-up. When a lower layer changes, use a cascading local rebase from the bottom (gh stack rebase, resolve conflicts, git add, gh stack rebase --continue, gh stack push) and re-seat upper layers before their lease-pinned pushes. Avoid the server-side 'Rebase stack' action for conflict recovery: it cannot resolve textual conflicts and creates unsigned commits. Without gh-stack, use git rebase --onto <new-lower-tip> <old-base> <upper-branch> for each affected branch, then push with an explicit ref and expected remote SHA using --force-with-lease. For gh stack checkout, do not rely on a bare number when a stack and pull request could share it: resolution tries a stack number first, then a pull request number, then a branch name. Use a pull request URL or explicit branch name when that distinction matters; if a safety hook blocks a push, verify locally and hand the operator the exact lease-pinned command rather than routing around the hook.
